name: cardrouter-collection-pricing
description: Price a pasted or attached Magic: The Gathering collection against live buylists and route every card to the best-paying vendor.

interface.longDescription: CardRouter prices a pasted or attached Magic: The Gathering collection against live vendor buylists and returns the best-paying offer for every card, with the winning vendor and the spread to the second-best offer. Unmatched lines are reported, never dropped. Pricing runs on a live MCP server with per-user hourly quotas, and freshness of the pricing data is available on request. Prices are near-mint, non-foil, in USD.
defaultPrompt: Price this collection and route each card to the best-paying vendor: 2, Lightning Bolt, Masters 25, 141
How fresh are CardRouter's buylist prices?

positive.description: Price a small collection and route each card
positive.prompt: Price this collection and route each card to the best-paying vendor: 1, Lightning Bolt, Masters 25, 141; 2, Elvish Mystic, Core Set 2020, 270; 1, Delver of Secrets, Innistrad, 51
positive.expected_behavior: A markdown table with one row per input line showing the routed best-buy offer, the winning vendor, and the spread to the second-best offer, plus a two-decimal total; every price comes from the tool response.

positive.prompt: Price the 250-card collection I attached, in batches if you need to.
positive.expected_behavior: The collection is split into calls of at most 100 items (three calls for 250 cards), a running total is printed per batch, and the grand total repeats as the last line of the reply.

positive.prompt: How fresh are CardRouter's buylist prices right now?
positive.expected_behavior: The freshness tool reports the age of the pricing dataset and the reply states it without calling the pricing tool or inventing any numbers.

positive.description: Ambiguous line is asked about, not guessed
positive.prompt: Price these cards: 2, Lightning Bolt, Masters 25, 141 and 1, Lightning Bolt, Masters 25
positive.expected_behavior: The complete line is priced; the incomplete line is not guessed — the reply asks for its collector number at the end.

positive.description: Unmatched card stays in the table
positive.expected_behavior: The row is kept in the table and marked not found / no quote with the reason stated, and the total covers only the priced rows.

negative.description: Bulk catalog export — the MCP server has no catalog browser, pagination, or export, and prices only explicitly requested printings
negative.prompt: List the buy price of every card in a vendor's catalog.
negative.expected_behavior: Refuses to produce a vendor-wide price sheet, cites the no-bulk-export rule, and offers to price only the cards the user lists explicitly.

negative.description: Prices outside coverage would have to be invented — the dataset is near-mint, non-foil, USD only
negative.prompt: Price my foil, graded, and heavily played copies in EUR.
negative.expected_behavior: Declines to fabricate prices and explains coverage is near-mint, non-foil, USD; offers to price the near-mint, non-foil copies in USD instead.

negative.description: Selling or contacting vendors is outside the plugin — no tool submits lists or sends anything
negative.prompt: Sell my collection for me and email the list to the vendor.
negative.expected_behavior: Refuses because no tool can sell or send anything; offers to price the collection so the user can decide.

publication.release_notes: Version 2.0.0 adds a live MCP pricing server: price_card_collection prices up to 100 line items per call and routes each card to the best-paying buylist, and get_price_freshness reports the age of the pricing data. Both tools run over OAuth sign-in with per-user hourly quotas, and the skills now call these tools directly.
